topic.title: Translation
topic.shortdesc: How translates DITA content with a steerable AI agent, reusing previous translations so that each job processes only the changes.

body.p: translates your DITA content into other languages by using an AI translation agent. Two features make it distinctive:

ul.li: It is incremental - records what it has already translated, so when you run translation again, it reprocesses only the files whose source content changed. You do not pay to retranslate content that has not changed.

It is steerable - Instead of using a fixed machine-translation pipeline, the agent follows guidance you provide, such as approved terminology, house style, and rules for your own DITA specializations, so output stays consistent across every language and translation job.

body.p: To try the full workflow, follow the Getting Started with Translation walkthrough, which uses a ready-made sample project.

section.title: The Translation Workflow
section.p: At a high level, translating content in works as follows:

ol.li: In your workspace, choose what to translate (one or more publications) and the target languages.
This starts a translation job, which the AI translation agent processes in the background, one target language after another.
When the job finishes, bring the translated files into your workspace.
Review the translated files and make any manual corrections you need.
Commit the result to your project's repository.

section.p: Because keeps a translation index in your repository, the translation state travels with the content, and later jobs retranslate only what changed. See Running an Incremental Translation.
Translation uses your organization's AI Credits, and its incremental design helps reduce costs by reprocessing only what changed.

section.title: A Steerable Translation Agent
section.p: You can control how the agent translates content for your project. For example, you can provide approved terminology, a style guide, or a list of strings that must never be translated. You can store this guidance in a file inside your project, and it applies to every translation job and every user until you change it. Because the agent reads whatever files you point it to, it can work with the formats your localization team already uses, whether that is a terminology file in a format such as TBX (TermBase eXchange) or the custom strings files behind an application's UI. See Customizing the Translation Behavior.

section.title: You Stay in Control of Your Content
section.p: Translation is a reviewed, reversible workflow. To translate content, sends source content to an AI provider engaged under zero-data-retention terms. The translated files are then proposed in your workspace for review before anything is committed. See Data Handling and Your Responsibilities for details about where your content goes and what to check before you commit.

Your translated files and translation state are stored in your own Git repository as plain, human-readable files, versioned under the same access control as the rest of your content. Nothing is locked inside a separate proprietary system.

section.title: Supported Languages
section.p: You can translate into any language identified by a BCP 47 language tag (for example fr, fr-FR, or de-DE). There is no fixed list of supported languages.

section.title: Current Limitations
section.p: The following are not currently supported:

ul.li: Markdown files. They are neither translated nor copied into the target-language folders. Only DITA content is processed.
Translating text embedded in raster images or other binary assets. Text inside SVG graphics is copied unchanged by default, but you can choose to translate it.

Exchanging translations with external translation management systems through XLIFF. Translations are produced and reviewed inside rather than exported to an external tool. If you want a translation agency or an in-house translator to handle a language, the agent can collect the source files that are not up to date into a folder that you send out (see Collecting Out-of-Date Content for an External Translation Agency).
Translation memories are not used during the translation process, nor generated afterwards.
